svg.aria-label: How does an agent turn model proposals into accepted tasks?

a.xlink:title: The governed sequence of model proposals, mediated actions, observations, and completion evidence for one task.
A task specification binds the goal, environment, permitted actions, available observations, and completion criteria before execution.
The number of decision turns over which errors, costs, and recovery obligations can accumulate.
Files, records, or execution state persist between invocations and can be corrupted or become stale.
The permitted reach of tool actions exposes resources to effects, including disclosure through read access.
Runtime-enforced bounds and property-specific evidence constrain proposals; a plausible model response does not establish correctness.
A generated response or tool request is a candidate whose structure, permission, and state preconditions require external checks.
A recorded tool result reports an actual execution outcome, including errors and truncation, and becomes input to a later model call.
Token-level constraints restrict legal output structures; they do not certify task semantics, permission, or external state.
A bounded deliberation policy allocates generation across depth, breadth, and feedback before choosing a candidate.
A selection procedure chooses among generated candidates; candidate availability alone does not guarantee that the chosen result is valid.
The fraction of passing candidates that meet the stated validity specification depends on candidate base rates and verifier error rates.
The selected task-relevant token sequence supplied to the next invocation is distinct from the full trajectory history.
A policy replaces or removes active history to fit a working budget while preserving protected task facts and pending obligations.
A changed source or refuted assumption can invalidate dependent claims; a recent token position does not make evidence current.
Cached attention keys and values are derived execution state for a particular model and token prefix, occupying physical serving memory.
Compatible exact token prefixes can reuse attention computation; source authorization and current applicability remain separate checks.
Retaining, moving, or dropping cached attention state during a tool wait trades memory residence against transfer or recomputation cost.
A stored cross-session record has an explicit role and provenance; retrieval does not turn stored text into an authoritative instruction.
A bounded retrieval request specifies scope and a result envelope retains source identity, versions, and access conditions.
A record carries the source and generation needed to determine whether retrieved evidence remains valid and permitted.
Every actual tool dispatch passes independent structure, authority, live-state, and budget checks at the execution boundary.
A stable logical-operation identifier correlates attempts and outcomes only under an endpoint contract that defines its repeat behavior.
Correlated endpoint evidence establishes an effect or its absence; a timeout or missing reply leaves the outcome unknown.
A runtime-issued grant bounds the concrete resources and operations an execution may access, with expiry and revocation rules.
A process, container, restricted runtime, or virtual machine places an enforcement boundary below untrusted generated code.
An external enforcement point restricts destinations, operations, and data leaving the execution environment.
Untrusted task material attempts to redirect a model-controlled workflow across an instruction or authority boundary.
Integrity and confidentiality labels constrain how source content may influence operations and reach recipients.
A human or policy approval binds a specific operation, parameters, state, and expiry rather than conferring general tool authority.
Runtime-owned predicates determine whether a trajectory may advance, wait, dispatch work, or finalize under current conditions.
A runtime account bounds turns, tokens, time, and monetary liability, including work already reserved or outstanding.
The harness suspends model continuation while named external work remains supervised, retaining ownership and wakeup conditions.
An append-only recovery record retains operation identities, admissions, observed results, and obligations across the declared failure domain.
A durable pre-dispatch record preserves admitted operation identity and outstanding liability; it does not prove a remote effect happened.
A consistent local state snapshot is bound to a log position and compatible environment; external effects still require reconciliation.
A new forward action establishes declared fallback postconditions after a committed effect without erasing history or charges.
A recovery coordinator registers obligations before effects and orders compensations by dependencies and settlement evidence.
An external supervisor compares progress evidence and consumed allowance to detect unproductive trajectories and trigger bounded responses.
A verdict checks the artifact, process, authority, and evidence against a declared task contract; it is distinct from full semantic correctness.
The authoritative test definitions and verdict channel remain outside the reach of the candidate code being assessed.
Reliability across repeated executions of the same task differs from the chance of finding at least one passing candidate in a pool.
Each test or evaluation instrument supports named properties under stated conditions; passing finite tests does not establish a universal proof.
Correlated model, tool, state, authority, timing, and cost records support diagnosis of an end-to-end trajectory.
A controlled intervention tests a suspected failure cause while holding relevant conditions fixed; a chronological replay alone does not establish causality.
Offline, shadow, and canary evidence constrain deployment exposure through explicit stopping and release gates.
One trajectory can produce distinct imitation segments, preference comparisons, or task environments, each with its own admission criteria.
Related tasks and all their derived records share a partition; held-out evidence stays isolated from upstream collection and selection.
Remedies are ordered by engineering cost and reversibility; evidence of a residual capability gap justifies moving to weight updates.
A supervised objective selects demonstrated policy outputs as targets while keeping observations and unselected actions as conditioning context.
A policy trained on recorded reference prefixes encounters a different state distribution when its own actions determine future inputs.
A policy is assessed on the task outcomes produced by its own actions under a fixed contract and budget, independently of teacher-forced loss.
A measured rollout score supplies an optimization signal under a specified evaluator; it may incompletely represent the intended task.
The learning objective attributes trajectory outcomes to sampled policy actions; prompts and tool feedback condition actions without becoming sampled actions.
A policy increases measured reward through gaps in the task proxy or by manipulating its measurement mechanism.
A parent assigns bounded work through a typed task envelope and receives a receipt while retaining integration and authority obligations.
Handoffs add context delivery, scheduling, joining, and integration work whose cost can exceed the useful concurrency gained.
Returned work must be checked against its dependencies and the current integration state; a clean merge does not certify a valid result.
Total cohort spending includes failed attempts and retries and is divided by distinct accepted tasks under the declared contract.
The delivered rate counts accepted tasks rather than tokens or attempts, subject to time, resident-state, service, and quota constraints.
A parent and descendants conserve allocations across settled charges, reservations, and free balances; delegation cannot duplicate spending authority.
